papers.title: MacroTox: A Macroscopic Graph Topology-Based Multimodal Learning Framework for Robust Molecular Toxicity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Despite breakthroughs in predicting acute organ toxicities, advanced computational models continue to struggle with complex, insidious end points like drug-induced bone toxicity. A fundamental limitation of most supervised pipelines is their failure to explicitly model intermolecular similarities during task-specific training. Neglecting this macroscopic topology of the chemical space leads to fragmented latent representations, poor generalization, and high false negative rates. To address this, we propose MacroTox, a macroscopic topology-driven multimodal deep learning framework. Beyond intra
papers.summary: MacroTox is a multimodal deep learning framework that explicitly models intermolecular similarities (macroscopic topology of chemical space) during training to improve molecular toxicity prediction, particularly for complex endpoints like drug-induced bone toxicity. By incorporating this macroscopic graph topology, it aims to produce more coherent latent representations, better generalization, and lower false negative rates than standard supervised pipelines.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study examines how the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs affects their ability to disrupt membranes, revealing that tail length is a key determinant of membrane activity. The findings suggest that carmofur and its analogs may act through noncanonical mechanisms beyond their known targets, such as acid ceramidase inhibition or SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibition.

papers.title: Quinazoline-tethered thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors: green synthesis, molecular docking, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-fused heterocycles have attracted considerable research interest in pharmaceutical, medicinal, organometallic, and materials chemistry. In this work, two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives were synthesized using choline hydroxide as an environmentally friendly catalyst. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT). Compound 11e showed the highest inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 0.599 µg mL-1 (1.305 µM). Molecular docking was performed to examine
papers.summary: This study synthesized two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives using an environmentally friendly choline hydroxide catalyst. The compounds were tested against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase, with compound 11e showing the strongest inhibition (IC50 = 0.599 µg/mL). Molecular docking was used to explore how these compounds bind to the enzyme.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and preliminary anticancer evaluation of diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives: in vitro, in vivo and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of cancer-associated mortality and morbidity worldwide, and there is a continued need for structurally diverse anticancer agents with improved properties. The present study reports a series of diphenylpropan-1-one (DPP) derivatives (4a-4i), rationally designed around a chalcone framework and synthesized via a three-step reaction sequence. The physicochemical and spectral characterization of the synthesized derivatives was performed using spectral techniques. Their anticancer potential was evaluated through a preliminary in vitro cytotoxicity screening against t
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of nine diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives based on a chalcone scaffold, followed by preliminary anticancer testing. The compounds were evaluated in vitro for cytotoxicity, with additional in vivo and in silico studies, suggesting potential as breast cancer agents. The work is an early-stage medicinal chemistry effort identifying candidate compounds for further development.

papers.title: Rational High-Throughput Screening of Cocrystals: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework Based on Morgan Fingerprints and Cross-Attention.
papers.abstract: Aiming to address the problems of high blindness in traditional screening methods, insufficient granularity of feature representation, and poor interpretability of existing machine learning prediction models in the field of cocrystal research and development, we propose a cocrystal prediction method based on Morgan fingerprints and the cross-attention mechanism. First, a high-quality cocrystal data set is constructed, and Morgan fingerprints are employed to characterize molecular structures. Subsequently, a fingerprint-driven cross-attention model is developed to capture the feature interactio
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning framework for predicting cocrystal formation that combines Morgan fingerprints with a cross-attention mechanism to capture interactions between molecular features. The approach aims to reduce the blind screening typical of traditional cocrystal discovery and improve model interpretability. It represents a methodological contribution to computational cocrystal screening rather than a new experimental finding.

papers.title: Deep learning of tautomer stability from crystallographic proton positions.
papers.abstract: Tautomerism plays a central role in molecular recognition, physicochemical properties, and chemical reactivity, yet rapid identification of stable tautomeric states remains a persistent challenge in molecular design and structure-based drug discovery. Quantum-mechanical approaches are often too computationally demanding for library-scale application, while rule-based and 3D-dependent machine-learning methods remain limited in either transferability or throughput. Here, we show that experimentally resolved hydrogen positions in the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD) provide a powerful large-sc
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates that experimentally determined hydrogen positions from the Cambridge Structural Database can be used to train a deep learning model that predicts stable tautomeric states of molecules. The approach offers a fast, transferable alternative to quantum-mechanical calculations and rule-based methods, enabling tautomer stability prediction at library scale for drug discovery and molecular design.

papers.title: xLSTM-based deep learning model for predicting anticancer Activity of pyrano[3,2-a]phenazine hybrid derivatives: Proof of concept.
papers.abstract: Finding novel treatments is a long and complex process involving extensive drug discovery, experimental testing, and preclinical research. Computational quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling can support this process by enabling rapid prediction of biological activity and identification of molecular features associated with activity. This study presents a proof-of-concept deep-learning-based QSAR framework for predicting the biological activity of pyrano[3,2-a]phenazine hybrid derivatives. The proposed framework combines an Extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM) architec
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study applies an Extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM) deep learning architecture to QSAR modeling, predicting anticancer activity of pyrano[3,2-a]phenazine hybrid derivatives. The work demonstrates that xLSTM can serve as a computational tool to support early-stage drug discovery by rapidly predicting biological activity and identifying activity-associated molecular features.

papers.title: S100A8/A9-TMEM24 axis drives podocyte injury by impairing autophagy: A novel theranostic target for early diabetic nephropathy.
papers.abstract: To establish a comprehensive theranostic framework for early-stage diabetic kidney disease (DKD) by validating serum S100A8/A9 as a highly sensitive diagnostic biomarker and exploring therapeutic strategies targeting the S100A9/transmembrane protein 24 (TMEM24) signaling axis to restore podocyte autophagy.
papers.summary: This study identifies serum S100A8/A9 as a highly sensitive biomarker for early diabetic kidney disease and shows that the S100A9-TMEM24 signaling axis drives podocyte injury by impairing autophagy. Targeting this axis restores autophagy, suggesting a combined diagnostic and therapeutic (theranostic) strategy for early diabetic nephropathy.

papers.title: FuTCM-PDD: a multi-level information fusion framework integrating KAN modeling and AutoML for phenotype-based drug discovery from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.abstract: Phenotype-based drug discovery has attracted increasing attention due to its critical role in first-in-class drug development and higher clinical translation rates. Chinese Materia Medica (CMM), with its emphasis on properties and efficacies, provides a unique framework for phenotype-oriented therapeutic discovery. We developed an AI-driven framework, FuTCM-PDD, that integrates CMMs, compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, CMM efficacies, and CMM properties to enable phenotype-based drug discovery. For drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction, a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) m
papers.summary: The authors present FuTCM-PDD, an AI framework that fuses multi-level data on Chinese Materia Medica—including compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, and traditional efficacy/property annotations—to support phenotype-based drug discovery. It uses a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for drug-target interaction prediction combined with AutoML to link traditional medicine knowledge to modern phenotypic screening. The work aims to bridge traditional Chinese medicine theory with computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I from Salvia miltiorrhiza: integrated in vitro and computational evaluation of their antidiabetic potential.
papers.abstract: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (Lamiaceae) is a traditional medicinal plant rich in bioactive tanshinones with diverse pharmacological properties. However, comparative information regarding experimentally measured activity and computational interaction profiles of individual tanshinones remains limited. This study aimed to compare cryptotanshinone (1) and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I (2), isolated from S. miltiorrhiza, using an integrated in vitro and computational approach. The compounds were obtained through activity-informed phytochemical fractionation and evaluated for inhibition of α-glucosidase
papers.summary: This study isolated cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I from Salvia miltiorrhiza and compared their antidiabetic potential using both in vitro enzyme inhibition assays and computational docking analyses. The work provides comparative activity and interaction profiles for these two tanshinones, highlighting their potential as α-glucosidase inhibitors.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Immune Dysregulation and Candidate Drug Targets in Endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder affecting 5-10% of women of reproductive age and is associated with chronic pain and infertility. While research has mainly focused on local lesions, systemic immune dysfunction is increasingly implicated in disease pathogenesis. This study employs single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from women with endometriosis and unaffected controls, combined with integrative analysis of publicly available datasets of menstrual blood and endometrial tissues, to uncover immune dysregulation and therapeutic targ
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from women with endometriosis and controls, combined with public datasets from menstrual blood and endometrial tissue, to characterize systemic immune dysregulation. The analysis identifies altered immune cell populations and candidate drug targets, suggesting that endometriosis involves broader immune dysfunction beyond local lesions.

papers.title: Physical priors improve performance of structure-based binding affinity models.
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug discovery is a widely used paradigm for the rational design of novel small molecule therapeutics. However, the benefits conferred by the use of structural information has seen limited adoption in machine learning, where ligand-only ("2D") models are still the industry standard for molecular property or binding affinity prediction. Structure-based ("3D") ML models for binding-affinity prediction promise to present a clear advantage, but have not yet overtaken existing 2D models. Here, we show that physics-based priors can improve predictive performance of structure-based mo
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates whether incorporating physics-based priors into structure-based (3D) machine learning models can improve binding affinity prediction, addressing the gap where 2D ligand-only models still outperform 3D approaches. The authors demonstrate that adding physical priors enhances predictive performance of structure-based models, suggesting a path toward more accurate rational drug design.

papers.title: From Glycan Biology to Drug Candidates: An Integrated Sialylation Niche Index and AI-Guided Therapeutic Framework for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) responds poorly (<20%) to immune checkpoint blockade. Since sialylation suppresses anti-tumour immunity through Siglec signalling independently of the PD-L1/PD-1 axis, we mapped its prognostic landscape in HNSCC by integrating prognostic modelling, molecular subtyping, and AI-guided drug discovery. Methods: Transcriptomic data from seven GEO cohorts and TCGA-HNSC (n = 501) were analysed with a 1204-gene sialylation compendium. The Sialylation Niche Index (SNI) was built in TCGA-HNSC from 117 machine-learning algorithm combinations (nomi
papers.summary: This study builds a Sialylation Niche Index (SNI) for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma by integrating transcriptomic data from multiple cohorts with a 1,204-gene sialylation compendium and 117 machine-learning algorithm combinations. The authors use this index for molecular subtyping and then apply AI-guided drug discovery to propose therapeutic candidates targeting sialylation-mediated immune suppression, a pathway that operates independently of PD-L1/PD-1. The work aims to address the poor response of HNSCC to immune checkpoint blockade by offering a new prognostic and therapeutic framework.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Diversity of Marine-Derived Streptomyces Natural Products: Integrating Genome Mining, Multi-Omics, and Translational Drug Discovery Strategies.
papers.abstract: Marine-derived Streptomyces are among the most prolific producers of structurally diverse and biologically active natural products. Adaptation to unique marine environments, including deep-sea sediments, hydrothermal vents, mangrove ecosystems, marine invertebrates, and hypersaline habitats, has promoted the evolution of specialized biosynthetic systems capable of generating a broad spectrum of secondary metabolites. These metabolites include polyketides, non-ribosomal peptides (NRPs), ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), terpenoids, alkaloids, and hybrid
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how marine-derived Streptomyces bacteria produce diverse bioactive natural products, shaped by their adaptation to extreme ocean habitats. It highlights how genome mining and multi-omics approaches can uncover cryptic biosynthetic pathways and accelerate translation into drug discovery. The paper frames an integrated pipeline from environmental genomics to therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: Benzamides of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles as Anticancer Scaffolds: Synthesis, In Silico and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Indoles and benzimidazoles are important nitrogen-containing heterocyclic scaffolds and are a cornerstone of synthetic drugs. In this study, benzamides of 2-aminophenylindoles and 2-aminophenylbenzimidazoles were synthesized and evaluated for their potential. Further, they were also subjected to computational studies for their ADMET profiling and binding with target proteins. Methods: The synthesized compounds were characterized by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR and electrospray ionization mass spectroscopy (ESI-MS). They were screened for their in vitro antibacterial activit
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of benzamide derivatives of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles and evaluated them for anticancer and antibacterial activity. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, tested in vitro, and subjected to in silico ADMET profiling and molecular docking against target proteins. Some derivatives showed promising anticancer activity, suggesting these scaffolds warrant further optimization.

papers.title: Cracking ERα Y537S Resistance: Explainable Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Molecular Dynamics Validation of Stable Candidate Ligands.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endocrine resistance due to activating mutations in the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), especially Y537S, is still a big challenge in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and there is a need to develop new small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome ligand-independent receptor activation. We used an integrated machine learning and molecular dynamics (MD)-based virtual screening (VS) approach to identify potential computationally prioritized hits of ERα Y537S in this study. Methods: The dataset (~3353 compounds) was characterized using molecular finger
papers.summary: This study combines explainable machine learning with molecular dynamics simulations to discover new small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome the Y537S mutation in estrogen receptor alpha, a key driver of endocrine resistance in breast cancer. The authors screened a library of ~3353 compounds and prioritized candidate ligands that remain stably bound to the mutant receptor, providing a computational pipeline for tackling drug-resistant ERα variants.

papers.title: Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Simulations Identifying Natural Product-Derived Cathepsin K Inhibitors as Potential Therapeutics for Osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis is a prevalent skeletal disorder characterized by excessive bone resorption and an increased risk of fragility fracture. Cathepsin K (CatK), a lysosomal cysteine protease predominantly expressed in osteoclasts, is an established target for anti-resorptive drug development. Here, an integrated computational workflow comprising virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, and drug-likeness/ADMET prediction was used to prioritize natural product-derived CatK ligands from th
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational pipeline—virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and ADMET prediction—to identify natural product-derived compounds that inhibit cathepsin K, a protease target for osteoporosis treatment. The workflow prioritized candidate ligands with favorable binding stability and drug-like properties, nominating them as potential starting points for anti-resorptive therapeutics. Experimental validation was not performed, so the findings remain computational predictions.

papers.title: Donor-Type-Dependent Heterogeneity of Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Lung Transplantation: A Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic Interaction Analysis of DCD Versus DBD Lungs.
papers.abstract: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and donation after brain death (DBD) donor lungs are widely used in lung transplantation yet managed as equivalent with respect to ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), despite fundamentally different ischemic backgrounds: warm ischemia in DCD versus neurogenic-inflammatory priming in DBD donors.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-cohort transcriptomic interaction analysis to compare ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) between DCD and DBD donor lungs in transplantation. It finds that IRI responses differ by donor type, reflecting distinct ischemic backgrounds—warm ischemia in DCD versus neurogenic-inflammatory priming in DBD. The results suggest donor-type-specific molecular mechanisms that may warrant tailored management strategies.

papers.title: Proteogenomic Profiling of Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Identifies Sex-Differential Proteins and Candidate Therapeutic Targets.
papers.abstract: Current biomarkers for idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) lack disease specificity and provide limited biological insight. We hypothesized that integrating population-based proteomics with genetic evidence would identify robust IPAH-associated proteins relevant to risk stratification, early detection, prognosis, sex differences, and candidate drug-repurposing opportunities.
papers.summary: This study integrates population-based proteomics with genetic evidence to identify proteins associated with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH), addressing the lack of disease-specific biomarkers. The authors uncover sex-differential proteins and candidate therapeutic targets, offering potential improvements in risk stratification, early detection, and drug repurposing for IPAH.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: This paper introduces KAN-GIN, a drug-target affinity prediction framework that replaces the standard multilayer perceptron in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation, paired with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was benchmarked on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ against a matched GIN baseline and other representative methods. The study tests whether adaptive nonlinear function learning improves molecular representation for affinity prediction.

papers.title: Multi-Endpoint Prediction of Bioactivity and ADMET Properties Coupled with Multi-Objective Optimization in Molecular Descriptor Space for Candidate ERα Antagonists.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Candidate estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) antagonists should combine strong inhibitory activity with favorable absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET)-related properties. This study developed an integrated framework for multi-endpoint prediction, multi-objective optimization in molecular descriptor space, and prioritization of feasible solutions. Methods: A dataset of 1974 compounds with 729 molecular descriptors, pIC50 values, and five binary ADMET-related endpoints was analyzed. Key descriptors were identified through two-stage cross-method and cross-e
papers.summary: This study builds an integrated computational framework that predicts multiple bioactivity and ADMET endpoints for potential ERα antagonists and then uses multi-objective optimization in molecular descriptor space to prioritize candidate compounds. Using a dataset of 1,974 compounds with 729 descriptors, the authors identify key molecular features that balance potency with drug-like properties. The approach aims to streamline early-stage drug discovery by ranking feasible ERα antagonist candidates before synthesis.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates the current state of molecular docking studies applied to natural products, highlighting that methodological quality remains highly variable despite advances in algorithms and AI. It examines how different natural-product classes and protein targets require tailored docking approaches and calls for standardized methodological guidelines.

papers.title: Retrieval-Guided Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Ebola Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computational drug discovery; however, its application to emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola remains challenging because of the limited availability of experimentally measured affinity data. To address this low-resource setting, we propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework that leverages BindingDB interactions to improve Ebola DTA prediction. The framework uses a two-stage strategy. In Stage I, source interactions are selected using random sampling, compound-similarity retrieval, protein-similarity retrieval,
papers.summary: This paper presents a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework for predicting drug-target binding affinity in Ebola, a setting with very little experimental data. It uses a two-stage strategy where relevant interactions from the large BindingDB database are selected via random sampling or compound/protein similarity retrieval to pretrain a model before fine-tuning on Ebola-specific data. The approach aims to overcome the scarcity of Ebola affinity measurements by borrowing knowledge from related drug-target interactions.

papers.title: Confidence-Gated Triage: Coupling Drug-Target Affinity and ADME-T Predictions to Prioritise Compounds for Docking.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics are accurate but computationally expensive, so the compounds entering them must be chosen well. The present study proposes CADT, a confidence-gated affinity-ADME-T docking-triage cascade that decides which compounds are worth docking. Methods: The gate combines an ensemble estimate of drug-target affinity with its epistemic uncertainty and an applicability-domain check. Predicted absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADME-T) developability is added as a soft flag. All components were trained on openly lice
papers.summary: The authors present CADT, a triage cascade that uses an ensemble drug-target affinity model with uncertainty estimates and an applicability-domain check, plus a soft ADME-T developability flag, to decide which compounds are worth sending to expensive docking. The goal is to prioritize compounds more efficiently by gating docking on confidence-aware affinity predictions and predicted developability.

papers.title: Integrated Machine Learning and Molecular Simulation-Guided Discovery of Novel Small-Molecule PD-L1 Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The programmed death-1/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) immune checkpoint is a key therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy, but small-molecule inhibition remains challenging due to its shallow and dynamic interaction interface. This study aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-guided workflow to identify novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface. Methods: A combined computational and experimental approach was established. A support vector regression-genetic algorithm (SVR-GA) model was trained on a dataset of 1385 known PD-L1
papers.summary: This study developed an AI-guided workflow combining a support vector regression-genetic algorithm model with molecular simulations to discover novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface for cancer immunotherapy. The approach addresses the challenge of the shallow, dynamic PD-1/PD-L1 interaction interface that has made small-molecule inhibition difficult.

papers.title: Big Data and Artificial Intelligence in Cancer Drug Discovery: Promise, Challenges, and Emerging Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Oncologic drug development is lengthy (~14 years) and expensive (~1.2 billion USD) with low clinical trial success rates (4.1%). Big data and artificial intelligence (AI) are widely proposed as tools to address these challenges. In this review, we examine the current performance and future potential of big data and AI applied to preclinical discovery and development, clinical trials, and the regulatory approval process. We first examine the data foundation required for effective AI, including data harmonization, data commons, and analytical tools. We then assess preclinical applications spanni
papers.summary: This review examines how big data and AI are being applied across the cancer drug development pipeline, from preclinical discovery through clinical trials and regulatory approval. It highlights the data infrastructure requirements (harmonization, data commons, analytical tools) needed for effective AI, while assessing current performance and future opportunities against the backdrop of lengthy, expensive, and low-success-rate oncology drug development.

papers.title: Development of an Interpretable QSAR Model for Predicting Coagulation Factor XIIa Inhibitors Using Ensemble Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Activated coagulation factor XII (FXIIa) is a component of the contact activation pathway and a pharmacologically relevant target in contact-system-associated processes. In this study, scaffold-aware and interpretable machine-learning QSAR models were developed for human FXIIa activity. Methods: Bioactivity records for the human single protein target CHEMBL2821 were retrieved from ChEMBL release 37. Modeling was restricted to exact IC50 measurements from assays explicitly referring to FXIIa, Factor XIIa, or activated Factor XII. Median-consolidated pIC50 values and two-di
papers.summary: This study developed interpretable machine-learning QSAR models to predict inhibitors of coagulation factor XIIa (FXIIa), a target in the contact activation pathway. Using IC50 data from ChEMBL and ensemble methods with scaffold-aware validation, the models aim to support drug discovery for contact-system-associated processes. The work emphasizes model interpretability to reveal structural features driving FXIIa inhibition.

papers.title: An AI-Assisted Workflow for Rapid Prioritization of FDA-Approved Drugs as HDAC3 Inhibitor Candidates for Drug Repurposing.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation through histone acetylation plays a critical role in gene expression and cancer progression. Because of its pivotal role in chromatin remodeling, Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) has become a promising therapeutic target. In this study, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven strategy was utilized to prioritize potential HDAC3 inhibitors among FDA-approved compounds to accelerate drug repurposing for cancer therapy. Existing HDAC3 inhibitors were identified in the BindingDB and were used to develop a machine learning (ML) model trained on the most potent inhibitors to identif
papers.summary: This study developed an AI-driven workflow that uses machine learning models trained on known HDAC3 inhibitors to screen FDA-approved drugs for potential repurposing as HDAC3 inhibitors in cancer therapy. The approach aims to rapidly prioritize candidate compounds, potentially accelerating drug discovery timelines by leveraging existing approved drugs.

papers.title: An Explainable Machine Learning-Based QSAR Framework for Predicting Thrombin Inhibitory Activity.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Public thrombin bioactivity records contain heterogeneous endpoints, replicate measurements, related chemical series, and potentially reactive compounds that may bias quantitative structure-activity relationship models. In this study, we developed an explainable, assay-aware, and leakage-safe machine learning framework for predicting thrombin-inhibitory activity. Methods: Exact Ki and IC50 records for human thrombin (CHEMBL204) were standardized, converted to pActivity, and aggregated using predefined criteria. The final dataset comprised 5189 unique compounds represente
papers.summary: This study builds an explainable machine learning QSAR framework to predict thrombin inhibitory activity from ChEMBL data, carefully standardizing and aggregating heterogeneous Ki and IC50 measurements into a leakage-safe dataset of 5,189 unique compounds. The work emphasizes assay-aware data curation and interpretability to reduce bias from replicates, related chemical series, and reactive compounds.

papers.title: AI-Powered Marine Drug Discovery: A Putative Dual c-Met/VEGFR2 Lead Candidate for Hepatocellular Carcinoma via Deep Learning and Multiscale Simulation.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality. The c-Met and VEGFR2 pathways synergistically drive HCC progression. Marine natural products offer chemically diverse drug reservoirs; however, conventional activity-guided isolation faces labor intensity, low throughput, and frequent compound rediscovery, limiting marine drug development.
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning combined with multiscale molecular simulation to identify a marine natural product as a putative dual inhibitor of c-Met and VEGFR2 for treating hepatocellular carcinoma. The approach aims to overcome the low throughput and rediscovery problems of traditional activity-guided isolation from marine sources. The work presents a computational lead candidate, though experimental validation appears limited to in silico methods.

papers.title: AlloPool is a deep learning framework that infers protein allostery from molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have transformed protein structure prediction and design. However, protein function is governed not only by static structures but also by the conformational dynamics that allow proteins to access distinct functional states. Predicting these dynamic transitions, central to many biological processes, remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-resolution experimental data, which limits the training of machine-learning models for dynamic and energetic property prediction. Here, we present AlloPool, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that in
papers.summary: AlloPool is a graph neural network framework that infers protein allostery directly from molecular dynamics simulations, addressing the scarcity of experimental data on protein conformational dynamics. By learning from simulation trajectories, it predicts dynamic transitions and energetic properties that static structure-based methods cannot capture. This offers a new computational route to understanding how proteins switch between functional states.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven decoding of maternal immune signatures in repeated pregnancy loss.
papers.abstract: Repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) is a multifactorial condition in which the underlying immunological mechanisms, particularly the disruption of maternal-fetal tolerance, remain incompletely understood. Although immune tolerance is critical for pregnancy success, the specific immune dysregulations contributing to RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies, have been difficult to characterize. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissues from RPL patients and first-trimester controls. Our analysis initially revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module of im
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissue from patients with repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) and first-trimester controls, combined with machine learning, to identify maternal immune signatures associated with the condition. The analysis reveals elevated expression of a transcriptional module in immune cells that may disrupt maternal-fetal tolerance, offering new insights into the immunological mechanisms of RPL in euploid pregnancies.

papers.title: Brewing Anxiety: Caffeine-Induced Thigmotaxis in Zebrafish Larvae.
papers.abstract: Thigmotaxis, or edge preference, is widely used as a measure of anxiety in vertebrate model systems. However, variability in this behavior limits its utility as a scalable measure for anxiolytic drug discovery. In the current study, we examine caffeine-induced thigmotaxis, using 5-day-old zebrafish larvae as a model system.
papers.summary: This study examines whether caffeine, a known anxiogenic compound, induces thigmotaxis (edge-preference behavior) in 5-day-old zebrafish larvae, aiming to assess the utility of this behavior as a scalable anxiety measure for anxiolytic drug discovery. The work addresses variability issues that currently limit thigmotaxis as a reliable screening assay.

papers.title: Exploring the Neuropharmacological Potential of Ligustrum sinense Relevant to Parkinson's Disease: In Vivo and In Silico Study.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are valuable sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in neurodegenerative disorders. This study investigated the antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities of Ligustrum sinense (L. sinense) leaf extract through in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. Antioxidant activity assessed by the DPPH assay demonstrated moderate free radical scavenging capacity (IC50 = 73.56 ± 2.18 µg/mL) compared with l-ascorbic acid (IC50 = 7.29 ± 2.86 µg/mL). Behavioral evaluations using the open field, hole cross, elevated plus maze,
papers.summary: This study evaluates leaf extracts of the medicinal plant Ligustrum sinense for antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities using in vitro, in vivo, and in silico methods, with relevance to Parkinson's disease. The extract showed moderate antioxidant activity and behavioral effects in rodent models, with computational docking suggesting potential MAO inhibition. The findings support further investigation of L. sinense as a source of neuroactive compounds, though the antioxidant potency was modest compared to standard ascorbic acid.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as potential aromatase inhibitors: Molecular docking, ADMET, Network pharmacology, Molecular dynamics simulation, and DFT studies" [Pharmaceutic. Sci. Adv. 4 (2026) 100108].
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.pscia.2026.100108.].
papers.summary: This is a corrigendum correcting the original article on computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as aromatase inhibitors. It does not present new scientific findings but rather corrects errors in the previously published paper.

papers.title: Computational evaluation of EPA-PC binding to GCase in neuronopathic Gaucher disease.
papers.abstract: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient acid β-glucosidase (GCase) activity and consequent accumulation of glucosylceramide. Current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies improve several systemic manifestations but have limited impact on neuronopathic disease, motivating evaluation of alternative molecular strategies. This study computationally assessed the interaction of EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, with human GCase (PDB ID: 2NSX). The protein structure was examined by Ramachandran analysis and hydroph
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and structural analysis to evaluate whether EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, can bind to the lysosomal enzyme GCase, which is deficient in Gaucher disease. The work aims to explore alternative molecular strategies for neuronopathic Gaucher disease, where current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies have limited brain impact. The findings suggest a potential binding interaction that could inform future therapeutic development, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Cutting-edge developments in computer-aided anti-HIV drug design.
papers.abstract: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS), caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), remains a major global public health issue. Current antiretroviral therapy (ART) does not fully eradicate HIV infection, and the virus can establish latent reservoirs in the body that are challenging to eliminate. Consequently, the development of new anti-HIV medications remains a critical necessity. Traditional drug development methods are time-consuming, financially demanding, and carry a high risk of failure. In contrast, computer-aided drug design (CADD) offers a promising alternative by leveraging
papers.summary: This review surveys recent advances in computer-aided drug design (CADD) approaches for developing new anti-HIV therapeutics, addressing the limitations of current antiretroviral therapy that cannot fully eradicate latent viral reservoirs. It highlights how computational methods offer faster, cheaper alternatives to traditional drug development pipelines for identifying novel anti-HIV compounds.

papers.title: Extra-nasal odorant receptors: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.abstract: Since the first demonstration of extra-nasal odorant receptor (OR) function of OR1D2 (hOR17-4) in human sperm, ORs have emerged as a widely distributed receptor family. ORs are now known to be belonged to a family of seven transmembrane domain G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) expressed across diverse extra-nasal tissues, including skin, gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, cardiovascular system, liver, immune cells, and tumors. In these tissues, ORs act as metabolite- and environment-sensitive sensors that translate chemical cues into tissue-specific signaling pathways that regulate proliferati
papers.summary: This review surveys the growing body of evidence that odorant receptors (ORs), a large family of G protein-coupled receptors, are expressed well beyond the nose—in skin, gut, kidney, heart, liver, immune cells, and tumors—where they sense metabolites and environmental chemicals. It discusses the molecular signaling mechanisms by which these extra-nasal ORs influence proliferation and other tissue-specific processes, and considers their potential as therapeutic targets.

papers.title: An interpretable consensus pipeline for candidate dopamine D2 receptor ligands.
papers.abstract: Machine learning accelerates GPCR ligand discovery but often lacks interpretability and struggles to generalise to structurally novel chemical space. We present an integrated framework combining ensemble learning, SHAP interpretability, and complementary structure-based analyses to prioritise putative candidates for the dopamine D₂ receptor (DRD2). Models were trained on 1247 curated ChEMBL compounds using Bemis-Murcko scaffold-split validation. Feature ablation showed that Morgan fingerprints alone were sufficient for classification (AUC = 0.910), whereas combined physicochemical descriptors
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable machine learning pipeline for identifying candidate ligands of the dopamine D2 receptor, combining ensemble learning with SHAP interpretability and structure-based analyses. Using 1247 curated ChEMBL compounds and scaffold-split validation, the authors found that Morgan fingerprints alone achieved strong classification performance (AUC = 0.910), suggesting simple chemical features may suffice for this task.

papers.title: FOXC1 drives lung cancer metastasis and functions as a target for AI-enabled anti-metastatic drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer metastasis remains the leading cause of treatment failure and death. Forkhead box C1 (FOXC1) promotes cancer progression, but its definitive mechanism in lung cancer metastasis and druggable potential remain unclear. This study aimed to clarify the mechanism and develop a FOXC1-targeted inhibitor.
papers.summary: This study identifies FOXC1 as a driver of lung cancer metastasis and demonstrates its potential as a therapeutic target. The authors use AI-enabled drug discovery approaches to develop a FOXC1-targeted inhibitor, providing a proof-of-concept for anti-metastatic therapy in lung cancer.

papers.title: Transforming Nanomaterials Development with Artificial Intelligence Techniques.
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into various scientific fields is reshaping traditional methodologies, and nanotechnology is no exception. This article explores the transformative impact of AI on nanotechnology, a domain focused on manipulating matter at atomic and molecular scales to develop novel materials with tailored properties. Historically, the discovery and optimization of nanomaterials relied on labor-intensive trial-and-error methods, often taking years to yield practical results. We examine how recent advances in AI particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning,
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, is transforming nanotechnology by replacing slow trial-and-error approaches to nanomaterial discovery and optimization. It surveys AI-driven methods for designing and predicting the properties of novel nanomaterials with tailored characteristics.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery: a deep learning paradigm shift in pharmaceutical research and development.
papers.abstract: Efficient drug discovery is essential to mitigate the high attrition rates and capital-intensive nature of traditional pharmaceutical research. Deep learning (DL) has catalyzed a paradigm shift, offering unprecedented computational capabilities to accelerate this process. This review systematically summarizes advancements in DL methodologies for drug discovery. First, the critical data foundations, Molecular Representation Learning, and core architectures underpinning artificial intelligence (AI)-driven therapeutics are elucidated, with a particular emphasis on the evolution of generative AI f
papers.summary: This review surveys how deep learning is transforming drug discovery, covering molecular representation learning, core neural network architectures, and generative AI approaches. It emphasizes the data foundations and methodological evolution driving AI-based therapeutic development. The paper is a broad synthesis rather than a primary research contribution.

papers.title: Network biology to artificial intelligence: building the next generation of predictive drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Drug discovery remains constrained by high attrition rates, prolonged timelines, and limited ability to translate molecular insights into effective therapies. Although reductionist approaches targeting individual molecules have delivered transformative medicines, successful patient-centric treatment remains a major challenge. Furthermore, increasing evidence demonstrates that therapeutic outcomes emerge from complex, dynamic, and context-dependent biological networks. Systems biology has provided a framework to understand these interactions, yet its predictive capability has been limited by bi
papers.summary: This review argues that drug discovery's high failure rates stem from reductionist single-target approaches and that therapeutic outcomes emerge from complex, context-dependent biological networks. It proposes integrating systems biology with artificial intelligence to build next-generation predictive drug discovery frameworks.

papers.title: RA-PLA: Retrieval-augmented graph convolutional networks for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) prediction is essential for computational drug discovery, yet existing deep learning methods typically employ a single globally trained model that fails to adapt to individual query samples. In this paper, we propose a novel end-to-end framework that retrieves hard protein-ligand pairs-samples whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels under manifold smoothness constraints-and integrates them via a semi-supervised graph convolutional network (GCN). For each query, we automatically construct a graph where nodes represent protein-ligand pairs and edges
papers.summary: The authors introduce RA-PLA, a retrieval-augmented framework for predicting protein-ligand binding affinity that retrieves hard protein-ligand pairs (samples whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels) and integrates them using a semi-supervised graph convolutional network. This allows the model to adapt to individual query samples rather than relying on a single globally trained model, potentially improving affinity prediction accuracy for drug discovery.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in non-small cell lung cancer: transforming diagnosis, treatment, and prognostic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by profound biological heterogeneity, frequently leading to late-stage diagnosis, recurrence, or metastasis. Conventional clinical pathways heavily depend on subjective visual interpretations, invasive tissue biopsies, and experience-based medical models that constrain individualized precision medicine. Identifying noninvasive, cross-scale tools for whole-disease-course assessment is critical for optimizing clinical decision-making and survival outcomes. This review critically synthesizes recent research progress and core algorithmic applicat
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in applying artificial intelligence to non-small cell lung cancer across diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis. It highlights how AI can address limitations of conventional clinical pathways that rely on subjective interpretation and invasive biopsies, supporting more individualized precision medicine. The authors argue that noninvasive, cross-scale AI tools are critical for whole-disease-course assessment and improved clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Identification of natural TLR4 modulators through network pharmacology and molecular modeling in SARS-CoV-2 Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection.
papers.abstract: Viral-bacterial co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii exacerbates hyperinflammation via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated immune pathways. Using network pharmacology, an integrated protein-protein interaction network identified 30 key inter-species hubs comprising viral, bacterial, and human host proteins, with TLR4 achieving a high MCC score (722), highlighting its high topological centrality as a host immune target. Virtual screen of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex identified three top candidates, CID5898023, CID5403474, and CID74977829, with docki
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to identify host proteins central to SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection, finding TLR4 as a top hub with high topological centrality. Virtual screening of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex yielded three promising candidate modulators (CID5898023, CID5403474, CID74977829) based on docking scores. The work proposes natural TLR4 modulators as potential therapeutics to dampen hyperinflammation in viral-bacterial co-infection.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK) to identify FDA-approved compounds that could be repurposed as antivirals. The approach targets an essential viral DNA replication enzyme, aiming to address the lack of effective mpox therapies.

papers.title: Large-scale virtual screening of 17,967 IMPPAT phytochemicals identifies multiple CDR1 binders and reveals Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a putative CDR1-GSC1 dual-target lead against Candida albicans with initial in-vitro evidence.
papers.abstract: The increasing incidence of antifungal resistance in Candida albicans, mainly mediated by multidrug efflux transporters and alterations of cell-wall biosynthesis, requires the discovery of new antifungal compounds targeting multiple pathways involved in resistance. In the present study, we employed an integrated computational-experimental workflow to identify potential antifungal phytochemicals from the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry and Therapeutics (IMPPAT) database. In the virtual screening, a total of 17,967 phytochemicals were screened against the ATP-binding cassette efflux tran
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study virtually screened 17,967 phytochemicals from the IMPPAT database against the Candida albicans efflux pump CDR1, identifying multiple binders and highlighting Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a dual-target lead that also binds GSC1 (a cell-wall synthesis enzyme). Initial in-vitro experiments supported its antifungal potential, suggesting a promising scaffold for overcoming antifungal resistance.

papers.title: Designing novel linagliptin analogs through combined generative artificial intelligence, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and binding energy estimation for targeting fibroblast activation protein.
papers.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is a highly specific biomarker overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts, making it a promising diagnostic target. Developing novel high-affinity molecular probes for FAP-targeted diagnostics remains an active area of research. In this study, an integrated computational pipeline combining generative artificial intelligence, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, binding energy estimation, and pharmacokinetic predictions was used to design and evaluate novel linagliptin-based compounds as potential FAP-binding analogs. From a preliminary
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline combining generative AI, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding energy calculations to design novel linagliptin-based compounds targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a cancer-associated fibroblast biomarker. The work identifies candidate FAP-binding analogs with favorable predicted pharmacokinetics, though experimental validation is not yet reported.

papers.title: Therapeutic Antitoxoplasmosis Potential of Garcinia cambogia: Evidence From In Silico and In Vivo Studies.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii, an opportunistic protozoan, is widely prevalent and poses potential health risks. Its treatment remains challenging with several side effects, urging the exploration of new, safe, and efficient drugs. We aimed to explore the therapeutic efficacy of the medicinal plant Garcinia cambogia (GC) against both acute and chronic toxoplasmosis. Sixty Swiss albino mice were allocated into five groups: I (healthy), II (model), III (spiramycin [SPM] treated, IV (GC treated), and V (SPM + GC treated). Each group is further divided into two subgroups receiving treatment at 4 and 42 days p
papers.summary: This study evaluated Garcinia cambogia (GC) extract as a treatment for Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice, comparing it to the standard drug spiramycin alone and in combination. Using both computational (in silico) predictions and in vivo experiments, the authors found that GC, particularly when combined with spiramycin, showed therapeutic potential against acute and chronic toxoplasmosis. The work suggests GC may be a safe, effective adjunct or alternative for treating this widespread parasitic infection.

papers.title: Design and syntheses of 4-aminoquinoline-thiazolidinone hybrids as anti-protozoal agents.
papers.abstract: Molecular hybridization is an effective approach employed to synthesize molecules that possess the ability to function as dual inhibitors, thereby addressing the issue of growing resistance. Resistance by the malaria parasite is one such example. Therefore, the study aims to develop hybrid compounds consisting of 4-aminoquinoline and 4-thiazolidinone, utilizing molecular docking for sorting, followed by synthesis and evaluation of their anti-malarial potential.
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized hybrid molecules combining 4-aminoquinoline and 4-thiazolidinone scaffolds, using molecular docking to prioritize candidates before synthesis. The hybrids were then evaluated for anti-malarial activity, aiming to create dual-action compounds that could overcome parasite resistance.

papers.title: Drug Repurposing for Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a prevalent chronic liver condition with limited approved pharmacotherapies. Drug repurposing offers a time-efficient alternative to de novo development, yet existing reviews often compile candidate compounds without critically appraising the methodological robustness, evidence quality, or translational barriers. In this review, we evaluated current repurposing strategies, including real-world data analyses, computational screening, and experimental validations. As a preliminary search for this review, we searched PubMed and clini
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates drug repurposing strategies for metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), covering real-world data analyses, computational screening, and experimental validation approaches. It highlights gaps in methodological rigor and translational barriers that limit clinical adoption of repurposed candidates. The authors argue for more robust evidence frameworks to advance repurposed therapies into practice.

papers.title: Cross-fusion of digital twins and artificial intelligence in diabetes: from mechanistic elucidation to full-cycle precision management.
papers.abstract: The integration of digital twins (DT) and artificial intelligence (AI) is driving a paradigm shift in diabetes mellitus (DM) care from traditional population-based, symptomatic intervention to a lifecycle-oriented precision management approach. This review systematically elaborates on the cross-disciplinary integration mechanisms of the two technologies. By integrating multimodal data and constructing physiologically constrained hybrid models, it achieves multi-scale mechanistic analyses ranging from single-cell β-cell protection to multi-organ complications at the basic research level. On the
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining digital twins with artificial intelligence could transform diabetes care from population-level symptom treatment to personalized, lifecycle-oriented precision management. It describes how multimodal data and physiologically constrained hybrid models enable mechanistic analyses spanning single-cell β-cell protection to multi-organ complications.

papers.title: Structure-based molecular modeling of a novel S-Remiketamine scaffold and derived arylcyclohexanone analogues: NMDA receptor dynamics, MM-GBSA ranking, and CES1-Oriented structural compatibility.
papers.abstract: Short-acting ketamine-related scaffold design remains an important medicinal-chemistry problem, but computational studies require conservative interpretation until receptor, enzymatic, and pharmacokinetic validation is available.
papers.summary: This computational study models a novel S-Remiketamine scaffold and related arylcyclohexanone analogues, examining their interactions with the NMDA receptor via molecular dynamics and MM-GBSA binding-energy ranking, plus structural compatibility with the metabolic enzyme CES1. The work is exploratory and the authors explicitly caution that the predictions require experimental validation of receptor binding, enzymatic processing, and pharmacokinetics before any conclusions can be drawn.

papers.title: From in silico prediction to experimental validation: Identification of drugs and novel synergistic combinations that inhibit growth of inflammatory breast cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing can accelerate the identification of novel therapeutic candidates for rare cancers such as inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), an aggressive type with limited therapeutic options. Here, we report an experimental validation study of compounds previously identified through two computational approaches: Literature Wide Association Studies (LWAS) and Gene Reversal Rate (GRR). Candidate compounds were tested using orthogonal cell viability assays in 2D models across IBC and non-IBC cell lines. In the SUM149 IBC cell line, repurposed compounds predicted from LWAS achieved a 70% succes
papers.summary: This study experimentally validated drug repurposing candidates for inflammatory breast cancer that were previously identified through two computational approaches (Literature Wide Association Studies and Gene Reversal Rate). Testing compounds in 2D cell viability assays across IBC and non-IBC cell lines, the authors confirmed that LWAS-predicted compounds achieved a 70% success rate in the SUM149 IBC cell line, and they also identified novel synergistic drug combinations. The work demonstrates that computational drug repurposing predictions can translate into experimentally confirmed growth inhibitors for this aggressive cancer type.
